reason: Both answers correctly identify confounding, endogenous placement/reverse causation, exposure and denominator problems, noise, ecological inference, spillovers, and extrapolation, and both propose credible staggered-rollout designs. A is slightly stronger because its proposed study more clearly specifies unit selection, stratified randomized timing, outcome and exposure measurement, adjacent-street spillovers, and analysis, while also giving well-defined quasi-experimental fallbacks and practical safeguards such as multi-year baselines, separating co-occurring interventions, and heterogeneity by lane type. B is also high quality, but its fallback design and robustness discussion are a little less fully specified.
